message.content:
In Ancient Greek, the person who establishes laws and orders is called a **law‑giver**.  
The Greek term for this role is **νόμογένεσθαι** (*nomogénesthai*), literally “to become law” or “to make law.”  

So, when you refer to the figure who creates laws in Ancient Greek, you can use the word **νόμογένεσθαι**.
